messages:
Jordan: did a quick bring-up of cust-marigold LoRA on base-xl int4. running the 'currency-conversion-edge' evalpack and seeing structured-json outputs malformed + wrong currency codes in conversions. opening a triage thread.
Kiki: can you drop the eval link and a tiny repro command?
Jordan: internal eval id: https://redwood.internal/evals/MG-202 (private)
Jordan: repro command i used:
```bash
./tools/quick_eval --model=marigold-lora-merged-int4 --eval=currency-conversion-edge --limit=300 --seed=3 --out=/tmp/mg_out.json
```
Jordan: failing example (expected structured JSON vs merged-int4):
```json
EXPECTED:
{"invoice_total": "1234.56", "currency": "USD", "converted_total": {"amount": "1012.34", "currency": "EUR"}}

MERGED-INT4:
{"invoice_total": 1234.5 6, "currency": "US D", "converted_total": {"amount": "1012.3", "currency": "EUR"}
```
Kiki: whoa malformed JSON (space inside "US D") and missing closing brace + space inserted in number. schema-validation rate drop?
Jordan: yes. Schema-valid percent dropped from 99.4% (fp32) -> 67.1% (merged-int4). For converted amounts exact-match fell 98%->61%.
Omar: sounds like tokenization + low-precision quantization combined with LoRA training on a compact-json serializer. did the customer train with a custom serialize step?
Jordan: they used a compact serializer that removes spaces between punctuation and fields; their LoRA learned on that distribution. our base tokenizer + merge expects standard spaced JSON tokens. merging caused token-id misalignment for tokens like "USD" vs "US" + "D" after int4 rounding.
Nina: quick experiments to run: 1) merged-int8 vs merged-int4 to isolate quant effect, 2) run merged-int4 but force customer's tokenizer/serializer at decode, 3) remap LoRA token ids for structured tokens using remap tool.
infra-bot: queued jobs: job-7011 (int8-ablation), job-7012 (int4+cust-tokenizer), job-7013 (remap+remerge). ETA ~22m.
Kiki: also test a 'schema-enforce' postproc (simple JSON repair + strict validation) to see if we can patch malformed outputs temporarily before rolling to customer.
Jordan: ran quick n=300 runs: fp32 schema-valid=0.994, merged-int8=0.987, merged-int4(default)=0.671, merged-int4+cust-tokenizer=0.885, remap+remerge-int4=0.962, int4+per-layer-clip=0.908.
Omar: remap+remerge helping suggests token-id mismatch is primary driver; quant amplifies it though. profiler shows large rounding shifts in embedding projection and output logits for tokens in position of structured markers ("\"", ":", "USD").
Nina: did we test KV-cache interaction? sometimes prefix caching with token-boundary differences shows different detokenization. add run with `--no-prefix-cache` to be safe.
Jordan: added that to the remap job. results updated: remap+remerge+no-prefix-cache = 0.967 schema-valid, EM_converted_amounts 0.94. small improvement.
Support: customer is concerned about wrong currency label (they saw "US D" once). recommend we block rollout and use fallback route to merged-int8 while we fix. need a one-paragraph explanation for CS.
Kiki: short-term plan: 1) block default rollout for this customer's merged-int4, 2) deploy remapped-int4 as canary behind feature flag with validation checks and fallback to int8 on schema errors, 3) provide CS note and ask customer about adopting standard serialize options.
Omar: medium-term: add token-alignment verification step in LoRA onboarding that flags structured tokens (quotes, colons, common currency codes) with >99.99% id overlap or auto-run remap. also add a structured-output evalpack to the onboarding CI.
Nina: long-term: consider a decode-time structured-token shim that maps few sensitive token ids per-customer before detokenization. cheap but brittle. prefer remap+remerge for correctness.
infra-bot: canary job created: route=customer/marigold/model=marigold-remap-int4, sample=1000, fallback=marigold-int8, monitor=[schema_valid_pct, EM_converted_amounts, currency_mismatch_rate].
Jordan: will draft CS blurb and PR for prod-config canary. posting artifacts to /artifacts/marigold/7011. will follow up when canary is live. :white_check_mark:
